say: You've heard you only use ten percent of your brain. Sounds like a superpower, right? Sadly, that's one hundred percent a myth.
Scientists have scanned working brains for decades. Over a normal day, every single region lights up. No dark, lazy ninety percent.
Even while you sleep, your whole brain stays busy, sorting memories and keeping you breathing. It doesn't switch off, it just changes mode.
Your brain is only about two percent of your body weight, but it burns around twenty percent of your energy. That's a very hungry organ.
And evolution hates waste. Your body would never keep feeding an expensive organ that mostly does nothing.
Doctors see it too. Damage to even a small area, like from a stroke, can cause real problems. There's no spare brain.
If you only used ten percent, you could lose the rest and keep about one hundred forty grams. That's roughly a sheep's brain.
So where did it start? A famous nineteen thirty six self-help book said William James claimed we develop only ten percent of our ability.
But James never gave a number, and nobody ever found Einstein saying it. Your brain is fully on, all day, every day.
